findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded directly in the Lambda function's environment variables, which means they are stored in the Terraform state, version control, and are readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration on the function. Static credentials in a Lambda also bypass the function's own execution role, granting whatever standing privileges the key holds.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables — which here contain secret credentials — are protected only by the default AWS-managed key, with no customer-controlled key policy or independent access boundary around the secret material at rest.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of support and no longer receives security patches for the runtime or underlying OS packages, leaving known vulnerabilities unpatched.

The function has no vpc_config block, so it executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary. Combined with the embedded static credentials, this gives compromised code an unhindered egress path for data exfiltration.
